answers.gloss: The transport circuit that an IP/VPN service is bound to ride over. It is owned and provisioned by the transport domain, while this model consumes it as the service's underlay; it is not merely an abstract binding record.
answers.example: IP service SVC-42 rides transport underlay U-7.
answers.relations: c.underlay carries c.service; inversely, c.service rides c.underlay. The underlay is below the IP-service layer and retains transport-domain ownership.

answers.gloss: A logical customer-site endpoint of an IP service, where that service meets the customer router. It is not, by definition, the physical transport-circuit demarcation, although implementations may colocate them.
answers.example: att-NY-SVC42 is the New York attachment of SVC-42 and carries C-VLAN 100.
answers.relations: Each attachment is of c.service and bears c.vlan encapsulation. It identifies a service endpoint at the customer/IP layer.

answers.gloss: The committed information rate guaranteed to customer traffic by the IP service, rather than the raw line rate or capacity of its transport bearer.
answers.example: SVC-42 has a CIR of 5 Gbit/s.
answers.relations: An attribute of c.service. It constrains guaranteed client payload throughput and need not equal the underlay's provisioned or physical line rate.

answers.gloss: The IP service's latency commitment, represented as a named SLA tier rather than merely a raw transport measurement.
answers.example: SVC-42 has tier T2, meaning latency no greater than 8 ms.
answers.relations: An attribute of c.service. The model does not encode a separate directionality relation; the commitment applies according to the service SLA, not intrinsically to the transport circuit.

answers.gloss: The resilience required by the IP service: its connectivity must survive a failure in the transport path supporting it.
answers.example: SVC-42 must remain connected after one underlay path failure.
answers.relations: An attribute of c.service expressing an observable service-layer survival requirement whose triggering failure occurs in the transport underlay. It does not itself denote a specific transport protection mechanism.

answers.gloss: The IP class of service applied to customer traffic, determining router scheduling and drop priority. It is not a physical transport protection or restoration grade.
answers.example: SVC-42 uses the gold class, mapped to a low-latency queue.
answers.relations: An attribute of c.service at the IP forwarding/QoS layer, with values such as gold, silver, and bronze.

answers.gloss: The customer VLAN tag used to identify traffic on a service attachment; it is an Ethernet/IP-side encapsulation object.
answers.example: C-VLAN 100 identifies SVC-42 traffic on its New York attachment.
answers.relations: c.vlan is on c.attachment, and the attachment bears it. It distinguishes customer traffic at the endpoint and is not a transport bearer.

answers.gloss: The end-to-end IP/VPN service delivered to the customer. It has logical customer-site attachments and rides a transport underlay; the transport domain itself sees the supporting circuit rather than this IP service.
answers.example: SVC-42 is a point-to-point IP service from New York to Frankfurt.
answers.relations: c.service rides c.underlay and attaches at c.attachment. Its service attributes include c.rate, c.latency, c.protection, and c.grade; its attachments bear c.vlan.

answers.gloss: A provisioned transport circuit carrying a client end to end across the optical core. It is the transport-domain underlay on which an external IP/VPN service can ride, rather than that IP service itself.
answers.example: CIR-7 runs from the New York hand-off to the Frankfurt hand-off and supports an external customer service.
answers.relations: It presents at m.handoff endpoints and is carried internally on m.bearer. The decisive experiment confirmed identity with c.underlay, including endpoint, connectivity, capacity, and layer relationships.

answers.gloss: The demarcation where a transport circuit presents to customer equipment. In this model it is expressed as a physical circuit hand-off.
answers.example: ho-NY-CIR7 is the New York port where CIR-7 meets the customer router.
answers.relations: It is an endpoint on m.circuit; no direct relation to m.bearer is modeled. Despite the physical-versus-logical wording, the decisive experiment confirmed identity with c.attachment while preserving endpoint and layer invariants.

answers.gloss: The committed client payload rate guaranteed end to end by the transport circuit, not the optical bearer's raw line rate.
answers.example: CIR-7 guarantees 5 Gbit/s of committed client payload.
answers.relations: It is an attribute of m.circuit. Whether it is semantically identical to the IP service's committed information rate remains to be tested because the owning layer differs.

answers.gloss: The one-way propagation delay of the transport circuit, represented as a measured numeric duration determined by its path.
answers.example: CIR-7's primary path has a measured one-way latency of 7.2 ms.
answers.relations: It is an attribute of m.circuit. Directionality is explicitly one-way; it is a raw transport measurement, not a named IP-service SLA tier.

answers.gloss: A transport mechanism protecting the circuit from fiber cuts or bearer/path loss by switching traffic to a diverse path.
answers.example: CIR-7 uses 1+1 path protection and continues over its diverse path after a primary-fiber cut.
answers.relations: It is an attribute of m.circuit and denotes the implemented transport protection mechanism, not merely an externally observable IP-service survival requirement.

answers.gloss: The circuit's transport quality grade, classifying its physical protection and restoration behavior rather than packet scheduling or drop priority.
answers.example: CIR-7 is platinum grade because it is dual-path protected; other values include gold and best-effort.
answers.relations: It is an attribute of m.circuit at the transport layer and is distinct from IP forwarding QoS.

answers.gloss: A physical optical wavelength on fiber that carries one or more transport circuits; it has no direct client-facing service meaning.
answers.example: The 193.1 THz wavelength on the New York–Frankfurt span carries CIR-7.
answers.relations: m.bearer carries m.circuit and supplies its internal optical path/capacity. Its relevant endpoints are optical transport nodes or span ends, not customer service attachments.
